module ara::log — Log and Trace

Specificatie: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf (R25-11) · 75 API-records

function: 65 enumeration: 3 class: 3 variable: 2 type alias: 1 struct: 1

User Guide Door AI gegenereerd

Automatisch gegenereerde beschrijving, inhoudelijk afgeleid uit de gerefereerde AUTOSAR-R25-11-documenten (SWS-specificatie en bijbehorende standaarddocumenten) — geen officiele AUTOSAR-tekst. Als interpretatie gemarkeerde uitspraken zijn conclusies uit de bronnen.

Rolle & Verwendungszweck

Der Functional Cluster Log and Trace (ara::log) stellt der AUTOSAR Adaptive Plattform und darauf ausgeführten Anwendungen ein einheitliches, hochperformantes Framework zur Erfassung von Diagnose-, Laufzeit- und Tracing-Informationen bereit SWS Log and Trace §1 “Introduction and functional overview”. Primäres Ziel ist es, Entwicklern, Testern und automatisierten Diagnosesystemen detaillierte Einblicke in das Systemverhalten zur Verfügung zu stellen, ohne das Echtzeitverhalten der Applikationen durch blockierende I/O-Operationen zu beeinträchtigen [SWS_LOG_00001].

Das Modul standardisiert die Protokollierung auf Basis des branchenweiten DLT-Protokolls (Diagnostic Log and Trace, gemäß ASAM/AUTOSAR-Standard). Es ermöglicht die Weiterleitung von Log-Nachrichten über mehrere konfigurierbare Ausgabekanäle (Senken), darunter ein zentraler DLT-Daemon (zur Übertragung über Netzwerkschnittstellen wie Ethernet oder SOME/IP), lokale Ringspeicher/Dateien sowie die Systemkonsole [SWS_LOG_00007] [SWS_LOG_00176]. Zudem unterstützt ara::log ARTI-Tracepunkte zur genauen Zeiterfassung und Ablaufverfolgung von Threads und Prozessen SWS Log and Trace §1.1 “Architecture overview”.

Architektur- und Schnittstellenverträge

Die Architektur von ara::log gliedert sich in Anwendungs-APIs, Kontextverwaltung und nachgelagerte Backend-Schnittstellen SWS Log and Trace §1.1 “Architecture overview”:

  • Initialisierung (InitLogging): Anwendungen können ihre Logging-Umgebung explizit über ara::log::InitLogging() konfigurieren oder sich auf die deklarative Initialisierung über das Manifest verlassen [SWS_LOG_00002]. Hierbei werden vierstellige App-IDs (z. B. "APP1"), eine Anwendungsbeschreibung sowie standardmäßige Log-Modi (LogMode::kRemote, LogMode::kFile, LogMode::kConsole) und globale Schwellwerte festgelegt.
  • Kontexte und Logger (CreateLogger): Jede funktionale Komponente innerhalb eines Prozesses fordert über ara::log::CreateLogger() einen Logger für eine spezifische Kontext-ID (CtxId, z. B. "SENS" für Sensorik) an [SWS_LOG_00005]. Logger-Instanzen besitzen eigene Beschreibungstexte und Schwellwerte (LogLevel) und sind referenzstabil.
  • LogStream und Formatierungsoperatoren: Log-Nachrichten werden über typsichere Stream-Operatoren (operator<<) formatiert [SWS_LOG_00129]. Logger stellt hierfür die Methoden LogFatal(), LogError(), LogWarn(), LogInfo(), LogDebug() und LogVerbose() bereit [SWS_LOG_00018] [SWS_LOG_00064]. Erreicht der geforderte Level nicht die aktive Filterschwelle, wird ein inaktiver Stream erzeugt, der alle Formatierungsoperationen ohne Allokationsaufwand überspringt.
  • RAII-Flushing und Pufferung: Das temporäre LogStream-Objekt sammelt formatierte Tokens und überträgt die serialisierte Nachricht beim Zerstören am Ende des vollständigen C++-Ausdrucks über Flush() atomar in einen sperrenfreien Lock-Free-Ringpuffer [SWS_LOG_00131] [SWS_LOG_00132]. Ein separater Hintergrund-Thread übergibt die Pufferinhalte via IPC an den DLT-Daemon.

Über DLT-Injektionsnachrichten kann der DLT-Daemon die Log-Level einzelner Kontexte oder der gesamten Applikation zur Laufzeit dynamisch verändern (SetLogLevel), ohne den Prozess neu starten zu müssen [SWS_LOG_00201] [SWS_LOG_00204].

Interaktionsfluss

Der Interaktionsfluss einer Anwendung mit ara::log gliedert sich in Initialisierung, Kontextregistrierung, Stream-Verarbeitung und asynchronen Backend-Transport. Zur Laufzeit erfolgt die Filterprüfung (Early Exit) direkt im Aufruferthread; erst bei Überschreiten der Schwelle werden Zeichenketten und numerische Werte in den Stream serialisiert und via RAII übergeben.

Interaktionsdiagramm: Initialisierung des Loggings, Erzeugung eines kontextbezogenen Loggers, RAII-basierte Nachrichtenformatierung über LogStream und asynchrone Weiterleitung an den DLT-Daemon sowie dynamische Schwellwertanpassung über Steuerkommandos. Quellen: [SWS_LOG_00002], [SWS_LOG_00005] und [SWS_LOG_00132].

Konfiguration & Fehlerbehandlung

Die Konfiguration von ara::log erfolgt primär im LogAndTraceInstantiation-Modell des AUTOSAR-Manifests. Dort werden AppID, Standard-Kontexte, Log-Senken (Remote, Console, File) sowie Puffergrößen und Verhalten bei Pufferüberlauf (Drop vs. Block) definiert [SWS_LOG_00205].

Hinsichtlich der Fehlerbehandlung verzichtet ara::log bei Standard-Log-Ausgaben bewusst auf Fehler-Rückgabewerte (Best-Effort-Prinzip), damit Logging niemals den primären Kontrollfluss unterbricht oder durch Ausnahmebehandlung gefährdet [SWS_LOG_00006]. Sollte der interne Ringpuffer voll sein, greifen standardisierte Strategien zur Vermeidung von Datenverlusten oder Deadlocks [SWS_LOG_20000]:

  • Pufferüberlauf (Overflow Handling): Dropping ältester oder neuester Nachrichten mit automatischem Einbetten eines DLT-Überlauf-Markers (Message Loss Counter), sobald der Puffer wieder aufnahmebereit ist.
  • Ungültige Kontext- oder App-Kennungen: IDs, die nicht den 4-Zeichen-ASCII-Konventionen entsprechen, werden auf standardisierte Ersatzbezeichner gemappt oder zur Compile- bzw. Init-Zeit abgefangen.
  • Verbindungsabbruch zum DLT-Daemon: Die Applikation puffert Nachrichten lokal bis zur konfigurierten Kapazitätsgrenze und schaltet bei fortdauerndem Verbindungsverlust automatisch auf Backup-Senken (z. B. Konsole) um.

FOLGENDE RICHTLINIEN SIND STRIKT BINDEND:
# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei ist Teil des Kuratierungsprozesses: Sie enthält die inhaltlichen
Leitplanken für alle KI-generierten Texte und Diagramme. Die maschinenlesbaren
Parameter dazu stehen in `ai/policy.json`; beide werden von
`ai_workflow.py auftrag` wörtlich in jeden Regenerierungsauftrag eingebettet.
Änderungen an Policy oder Richtlinien ⇒ `version` in `policy.json` erhöhen;
`ai_workflow.py status` zeigt dann, welche Fragmente noch mit einer älteren
Version erzeugt wurden.

## Geltungsbereich und Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch (`site.json → sprachen.kanonisch`). KI-Inhalte
  werden ausschließlich deutsch erzeugt; die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter
  Schritt (i18n_*.py) und niemals Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und `[SWS_…]`-Kennungen bleiben
  in jeder Sprache unverändert.

## Strukturelle Invarianten

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai` für
  Abschnitte, `ai usage` für Verwendungshinweise an Records, `ai module-guide`
  für Modul-Leitfäden) mit Badge und abschließender `<p class="ai-note">`
  (KI-Hinweis). Bestehende Fragmente sind die Referenz.
- Fragmente liegen unter `content/ai/<seiten-verzeichnis>/` und heißen
  `rec_<ELEMENT-ID>_<NN>.html` (an ein Spezifikationselement gebunden) oder
  `main_<NN>.html` (seitenbezogen).

## Belegpflicht und Quellen

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist mit `[SWS_…]`/`[RS_…]`-Zitat zu belegen
  (`policy.zitierpflicht`); Zitate verlinken auf das Quelldokument (PDF mit
  `#nameddest`), Richtwert `policy.relevanz.min_zitate_je_absatz`.
- Es dürfen nur Dokumente aus dem Quellenregister `ai/quellen.json` verwendet
  werden. Neue Quellen werden zuerst dort registriert (id, titel, typ, url).
- Aus Quellen extrahierte Einzelaussagen, auf die sich ein Text stützt, werden
  in der Trace unter `wissen[]` festgehalten: `{"aussage": …, "quelle": <id>,
  "fundstelle": …}`.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Spezifikation schweigt, darf die KI Lücken mit Annahmen schließen —
  höchstens `policy.annahmen.budget_je_text` pro Text bzw.
  `budget_je_diagramm` pro Diagramm.
- Jede Annahme wird (a) im Text als Interpretation erkennbar formuliert und
  (b) in der Trace unter `annahmen[]` protokolliert:
  `{"annahme": …, "begruendung": …}`.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekuliert.

## Diagramm-Entscheidung

Ein Diagramm wird nur eingefügt, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet
(`policy.diagramme`):

- Sequenzdiagramm (`.seq.json`): Abläufe mit ≥ `sequenz_ab_schritten`
  Schritten oder nicht offensichtlicher Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Strukturdiagramm (`.dot`): ≥ `kontext_ab_beteiligten` beteiligte
  Komponenten oder nicht-triviale Vererbungs-/Abhängigkeitscluster.
- Zustandsdiagramm (`.dot`): Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Die Entscheidung („warum dieses Diagramm, warum diese Form“), etwaige
Annahmen und das Denk-Transkript zur Quellenerstellung gehören in die Trace
unter `diagramme["<quellpfad>"]` — nicht ins HTML. Diagrammquellen liegen als
`<fragment-stem>.<diag-id>.dot|.seq.json` neben dem Fragment (inline) bzw.
unter `diagrams/` (seitenweite Diagramme); gerendert wird mit
`render_diagrams.py`. Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert.

Antworte AUSSCHLIESSLICH im validen JSON-Format gemäß folgendem Schema:
Erwartete Ausgabe: JSON-Datei mit demselben Namen wie dieser Auftrag,
Endung .out.json statt .json, im selben Verzeichnis. Aufbau:
{"ergebnisse": [{
  "fragment":  "<wie im Auftrag>",
  "html":      "<vollständiges <div class=\"ai …\">-Fragment, deutsch>",
  "diagramme": {"<pfad relativ zu _src>": "<Quelltext .dot | .seq.json>"},
  "trace": {"prompt": "<der bearbeitete Auftragstext>",
            "modell": "<verwendetes Modell>",
            "wissen":   [{"aussage": "...", "quelle": "<dok-id>", "fundstelle": "..."}],
            "annahmen": [{"annahme": "...", "begruendung": "..."}],
            "transkript": "<Denkprozess/Begründungsgang dieses Laufs>",
            "diagramme": {"<pfad>": {"entscheidung": "...", "annahmen": [...],
                                     "transkript": "..."}}}}]}
Alle Vorgaben aus policy und richtlinien sind bindend (Belegpflicht,
Annahmen-Budget, Diagramm-Kriterien, ai-note, deutsche Sprache).

        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Set the message’s privacy level. A program that calls this function with a T that is neither an integral nor an enum type is ill-formed. Only the lower 8 bits of value are used, any higher-level bits are ignored.</p></div>",

        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\">template &lt;typename MsgId, typename... Params&gt; void TraceArti (const MsgId &amp;msg_id, const Params &amp;...                       params) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Handles a modeled message, specific to the used trace tool. This function is only called internally by the Logger framework when switching between Log and TraceArti. It represents the interface to trace tools. The runtime overhead of this function shall be kept as minimal as possible, e.g. by using specializations based on the MsgId.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"

      "source_page": 7,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[9] Specification of Operating System Interface\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_OperatingSystemInterface\n7 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P8_09",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 8,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n1 Introduction and functional overview\nThis specification specifies the functionality of the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\nLog and Trace\n.\nThe\nLog and Trace\nprovides interfaces for\nAdaptive Application\ns to forward\nlogging information onto the communication bus, the console, to the file system or to\nARTI-trace. Each of the provided logging information has its own severity level. For\neach severity level, a separate method is provided to be used by applications or\nAdap-\ntive Platform Service\ns, e.g. ara::com. In addition, utility methods are provided\nto convert decimal values into the hexadecimal numeral system, or into the binary nu-\nmeral system.\nTo pack the provided logging information into a standardized delivery and presentation\nformat, a protocol is needed. For this purpose, the\nLT protocol\ncan be used, which\nis standardized within the AUTOSAR consortium.\nThe\nLT protocol\ncan add additional information to the provided logging informa-\ntion. This information can be used by a\nLogging client\nto relate, sort or filter the\nreceived logging frames.\nDetailed information regarding the use cases and the\nLT protocol\nitself are provided\nby the PRS Log and Trace protocol specification. For more information regarding the\nLT protocol\nrefer to [1]."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P8_10",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 8,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 1.1: Architecture overview\nThe\nARTI-trace\nmethods are integrated in the ara::log Functional Cluster. The sup-\nport of\nARTI-trace\nfunctionality of non AUTOSAR applications or services is handled\nby adapters (i.e. OS/ara::log Adapter).\nFurthermore, this document introduces additional specification extensions for the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform Log and Trace\n.\n8 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"
    },

      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 10,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n3 Input documents & related standards and norms\n3.1 Input documents\nNOTE: [4, RS-RSGeneral] is listed here as an input document because it applies to\nSWS LogAndTrace as well as to all SWS documents of the Adaptive Platform. Since it\nincludes only non-functional requirements the tracing is not necessary.\n3.2 Further applicable specification\nAUTOSAR provides a core specification [5] which is also applicable for\nLog and\nTrace\n. The chapter General requirements for all Functional Clusters of this specifica-\ntion shall be considered as an additional and required specification for implementation\nof\nLog and Trace\n.\n10 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P11_16",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 11,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4 Constraints and assumptions\n4.1 Known limitations\nThe provided\nLogging framework\nAPI is designed to be independent from the un-\nderlying\nLogging back-end\nimplementation and as such doesn't impose limitations.\n4.2 Applicability to car domains\nNo restrictions to applicability.\n11 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P12_17",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 12,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n5 Dependencies to other Functional Clusters\nThis chapter provides an overview of the dependencies to other Functional Clusters in\nthe AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform. Section 5.1 Provided Interfaces lists the interfaces\nprovided by\nLog and Trace\nto other Functional Clusters. Section 5.2 Required In-\nterfaces lists the interfaces required by\nLog and Trace\n.\nA detailed technical architecture documentation of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform is\nprovided in [6].\n5.1 Provided Interfaces"
    },

Table 5.1 provides a complete list of in-\nterfaces provided to other Functional Clusters within the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform."

    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P16_33",
      "source_element": "SWS_LOG_00206",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 16,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_LOG_20001] [SWS_LOG_20002]\n[SWS_LOG_20003] [SWS_LOG_20004]\n[SWS_LOG_20005]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P17_34",
      "source_element": "SWS_LOG_00001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 17,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7 Functional specification\nThis specification defines the usage of the defined C++\nLogging API\nfor the\nLog\nand Trace\n.\nAdaptive Application\ns can use these functions to forward\nLog\nmessage\ns to various sinks, for example the network, a serial bus, the console or the\nfile system.\nThe following functionalities are provided:\n1) Methods for initializing the\nLogging framework\n(see 7.2.6)\n2) Utility methods to convert decimal values into hexadecimal or binary values (see\n7.3.1.2)\n3) Automatic timestamping of\nLog message\ns (see 7.5)\n4) Log and trace network bandwith limitation (see chapter 7.6)\nAdaptive Application\ns and Functional Clusters can startup (see 7.1.1)\nand shutdown (see 7.1.2) all Functional Clusters with direct ARA interfaces\n(e.g. the\nLogging framework\n), by calling\nara::core::Initialize()\nor\nara::core::Deinitialize()\n.\n7.1 Functional Cluster Lifecyle\n7.1.1 Startup\nIn order to initialize the Logging framework, mandatory information needs to be pro-\nvided to the\nLogging framework\n. These information are extracted from the appli-\ncation execution manifest and the AUTOSAR Meta-Model. The execution manifest pa-\nrameter\nExecutable.loggingBehavior\ndefines if the logging functionality should\nbe initialized. Initialization of the Logging framework (via\nara::core::Initialize\n)\nis mandatory before usage of any\nara::log\nAPI. Failure to do so will result in unde-\nfined behavior.\n[SWS_LOG_00001]\n⌈\nLog message logged before the\nLogging framework\nis able\nto process them (e.g. daemon communication is not established) shall be queued.\nThe queue size is defined by\nLogAndTraceInstantiation\n.queueSize. If this size\nis exceeded the oldest entries shall be discarded.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003, RS_LT_00052)\n7.1.2 Shutdown\nNote\n: after\nara::core::Deinitialize()\nis called, the application has to stop us-\ning the logging api. It also means that no futher messages can be logged anymore.\n17 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P18_35",
      "source_element": "SWS_LOG_00123",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 18,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_LOG_00123]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nWhen\nara::core::Deinitialize()\nis called, the\nLogging framework\nshall pass all queued messages to configured log sinks.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nLT_00003)\n7.2 Necessary Parameters and Initialization\nThe concept of identifying the user application:\nTo be able to distinguish the logs of different application instances within a system (e.g.\nan ECU or even the whole vehicle), every\nApplication process\n, in that system,\nhas to get a particular ID and a description.\nThe concept of log contexts:\nIn order to be able to distinguish the logs from different logical groups within an\nAppli-\ncation process\n, for every context within an\nApplication process\na particular\nID and a description has to be assigned. Every\nApplication process\ncan have an\narbitrary number of contexts.\nMachine\n-specific configuration settings for the Log and Trace functional cluster are\ncollected in\nLogAndTraceInstantiation\n. The\nApplication process\nes using\nthe\nLogging framework\nneed to supply the following configuration through the ap-\nplication execution manifest:\n•\nApplication ID\n•\nApplication description\n•\nThe default log level, if not set through the manifest a default predefined value is\nset\n•\nThe log mode\n•\nThe log file path, in case of a specific log mode that indicates logging to a file\nThe\nApplication process\nusing the\nLogging framework\ncreates a\nLogging\ninstance\nper context. The context is defined at creation of the\nLogging instance\nand the following information should be provided:\n•\nContext ID\n•\nContext description\n•\nThe default log level, if not set through the manifest a default predefined value is\nset\n7.2.1 Application ID\nThe Application ID is an identifier that allows to associate generated logging informa-\ntion with its user application. The Application ID is passed as a string value. Depend-\ning on the\nLogging framework\nactual implementation, i.e.\nLogging back-end\n,\n18 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P19_36",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 19,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nthe length of the Application ID might be limited. To be able to unambiguously as-\nsociate the received logging information to the origin, it is recommended to assign\nunique Application IDs within one ECU. There is no need for uniqueness of Application\nIDs across ECUs as the ECU ID will be the differentiator. The system integrator has\nthe overall responsibility to ensure that each\nApplication process\ninstance has\na unique Application ID. By having this value defined in the manifest the integrator is\nable to perform consistency checks. The\napplicationId\nin the\nDltApplication\nidentifies the application instance and is put as\nApplicationId\ninto the log and trace\nmessage.\nNote\n:\nThe Application IDs are unique IDs per\nApplication process\n, meaning if the same\nApplication process\nis started multiple times it shall have an own ID per instance.\nThe length limits of the Application ID apply only to version-1 of the PRS LogAndTra-\nceProtocol.\n7.2.1.1 Application Description\nSince the length of the Application ID can be quite short, an additional descriptive text\ncan be provided. This description is passed as a string and the maximum length is im-\nplementation dependent. The\napplicationDescription\nin the\nDltApplication\nis an optional setting that allows to describe the\napplicationId\nas descriptive text.\n7.2.2 Default Log Level\nThe\nLog severity level\nrepresents the severity of the log messages. Severity lev-\nels are defined in chapter 7.3.\ndefaultLogThreshold\nin the\nDltLogSink\ndefines\nthe initial log reporting level for the application instance.\nEach initiated log message is qualified with such a severity level. The default\nLog\nseverity level\nis set through the application configuration per\nApplication\nprocess\n. The\nLog severity level\nacts as a reporting filter. Only log messages\nhaving a higher or the same severity will be processed by the\nLogging framework\n,\nwhile the others are ignored.\nThe default\nLog severity level\nis the initially configured log reporting level for a\ncertain\nApplication process\n, though it can be overriden per context.\nThe\nApplication process\nwide log reporting level shall be adjustable during run-\ntime. The realization is an implementation detail of the underlying back-end. E.g.\nremotely via a\nLogging client\nfor example\nDLT\nViewer. The same applies for the\ncontext reporting level.\nThe design rationale for providing an initial default\nLog severity level\napplication\nwide against having per context default\nLog severity level\ns is the following:\n19 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P20_37",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 20,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n•\nIt simplifies the API usage. Otherwise the user will have to define a context default\nLog severity level\nfor each group before using the API.\n•\nThe context separation of\nLog message\ns is possible during runtime.\n7.2.3 Log Mode\nDepending on the\nLogging framework\nimplementation, the passed logging infor-\nmation can be processed in different ways. The destination (the\nLog message\nsink)\ncan be the console output, a file on the file system or the communication bus. The\nsystem integrator is responsible to populate this information in the machine manifest.\nA direct API for dynamically changing this value for development purposes is provided.\nIn the AUTOSAR Meta-Model the\ncategory\nof\nDltLogSink\nis equivalent to the log\nmode described here, for more information see [3]. The\ncategory\nof\nDltLogSink\ndefines the destination to which the log messages will be forwarded."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P21_38",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 21,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.3.1 Log File Path\nIn case the log mode is set to log to a file, a destination directory path needs to be\nprovided.\npath\nin the\nDltLogSink\ndefines the destination file to which the logging\ninformation is passed. This option is provided for development, integration and proto-\ntyping purposes and is not suitable for production.\n7.2.4 Context ID\nThe Context ID is an identifier that is used to logically group logging information within\nthe scope of an\nApplication process\n. The Context ID is passed as a string value.\nDepending on the actual implementation of the\nLogging back-end\n, the length of the\nContext ID might be limited. Context ID is unique in the scope of an\nApplication\nprocess\nand as such the developer is responsible for assigning it and this informa-\ntion is not modeled in the manifest. There is no need for uniqueness of Context IDs\nacross multiple different\nApplication process\nes as the Application ID will be the\ndifferentiator.\nNote\n:\nSpecial attention should be paid to library components. The libraries are meant to\nbe used by\nApplication process\nes and therefore are running within the\nAppli-\ncation process\n' scope. Logging executed from those libraries will end up inside\nthe scope of the parent\nApplication process\n. In order to distinguish the internal\nlibrary logs from the\nApplication process\nlogs or from other library logs within\nsame process, each library might need to reserve its own Context IDs system wide \nat least when it shall be used by more than one\nApplication process\n.\nThe length limits of the Cotext ID apply only to version-1 of the PRS LogAndTracePro-\ntocol.\n7.2.5 Context Description\nSince the length of the Context ID can be quite short, an additional descriptive text must\nbe provided. This Context description is passed as a string. The maximum length of\nthe Context description is implementation dependent.\n7.2.6 Initialization of the Logging framework\nThe Application ID and description are used to identify and to associate the provided\nlogging information with the exact process. The log mode and sink information defines\nwhere the logging information is routed. Possible destinations are the console, the file\nsystem or the communication bus.\n21 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P22_39",

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nFrom the\nApplication process\n' perspective, the\nLogging framework\nis intial-\nized and a logger instance is created when an\nApplication process\ndecides to\nregister a logging context. These contexts are used to logically cluster logging infor-\nmation.\n[SWS_LOG_00002]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nIn case of any errors occurring inside the\nLogging\nframework\nor underlying system, it is intended to not bother the\nApplication pro-\ncess\nand silently discard the function calls. For this purpose, the relevant interfaces\nneither specify return values nor throw exceptions.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003)\n[SWS_LOG_00004]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nThe\nLogging framework\nshall be initialized if the Ex-\necutable has a\nPortPrototype\nthat is typed by a\nLogAndTraceInterface\n.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nLT_00003, RS_LT_00047, RS_LT_00048)\n[SWS_LOG_00005]\n⌈\nThe function\nara::log::CreateLogger\nshall create a\nara::\nlog::Logger\ninstance internally inside the\nLogging framework\nand return it as\nreference to the using application. Before a\nLog message\ncan be processed, at least\none\nara::log::Logger\nshall be available.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003, RS_LT_00050)\nNote:\nThis strong ownership relationship of contexts to the\nLogging framework\nensure\ncorrect housekeeping of the involved resources. The design rationale is, once a\ncontext is registered against the\nLogging back-end\n, its lifetime must be ensured\nuntil the end of the\nApplication process\n.\n[SWS_LOG_00006]\n⌈\nThe call to\nara::log::CreateLogger\nshall create a\nara::\nlog::Logger\ninstance with the given context ID, context description, and log level\nthreshold.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003, RS_LT_00050)\n[SWS_LOG_00253]\n⌈\nThe call to\nara::log::CreateLogger\nshall create a\nara::\nlog::Logger\ninstance with the given context ID and context description, and a log\nlevel threshold that is taken from\nDltLogSink.defaultLogThreshold\nin the Man-\nifest for the\nDltLogSink\nthat corresponds to the given context ID. If no such entry\nexists in the Manifest, then\nLogLevel::kWarn\nshall be used.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003, RS_-\nLT_00050)\n[SWS_LOG_00254]\n⌈\nThe call to\nara::log::Logger::SetThreshold\nshall set the\nloglevel threshold for the\nara::log::Logger\ninstance to the given level.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_-\n00003, RS_LT_00050)\n[SWS_LOG_00007]\n⌈\nApplication process\nes should be able to check if a desired\nLog severity level\nis configured through the function\nara::log::Logger::\nIsEnabled\n. This mechanism conserves CPU and memory resources that are used\nduring preparation of logging information, as this logging information is filtered by the\nLogging framework\nlater on.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003, RS_LT_00045)\n22 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P23_40",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 23,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.3 Log Messages\nLog messages can generally be output to different targets. The Log and Trace Func-\ntional Cluster supports these logging targets:\n- the console\n- a file on a local file system\n- a network\nMost of the discussion in this section assumes that messages are being output to a\nnetwork, as this use case requires the additional consideration of minimizing network\nload.\nThe Log And Trace Functional Cluster offers two principal classes of log messages:\nModeled\nand\nNon-Modeled\nmessages. Both these support adding one or more argu-\nments to a log message. A log message without any arguments serves no purpose\nand is discarded.\nNon-Modeled\nmessages are the traditional way of composing log messages: All ar-\nguments of the message are added to an internal message buffer and then eventually\nserialized for output, either to a console/file, or via network. All parts of the messages\nwill be sent via network. In the DLT protocol, these messages are called verbose\nmessages.\nModeled\nmessages are designed to reduce traffic on the network, by omitting certain\nstatic (i.e. unchanging) parts of a message from the network. As the name suggests,\nthese parts are instead added to the application ARXML model. In the DLT protocol,\nthese messages are called non-verbose messages. A log message viewer applica-\ntion is able to display the full message by combining the static parts from the model\nwith the dynamic parts from the received message.\nNon-modeled messages are mainly used during development, as the information re-\nquired for the modeled messages may not be available at that time. However, non-\nmodeled messages can impose a high load on the network, making modeled mes-\nsages usually the preferred choice in production systems.\nThe\nara::log\nFunctional Cluster supports defining and using both modeled and non-\nmodeled messages in a single application at the same time.\nException safety\n: All\nLog\n*\n()\ninterfaces are designed to guarantee no-throw behav-\nior. This applies for the whole\nLogging API\n.\n23 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P24_41",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.3.1 Non-modeled messages\nThe\nara::log\nFunctional Cluster defines a Builder-pattern inspired set of APIs for\nconstructing non-modeled messages. The\nara::log::Logger::WithLevel\nmem-\nber function is used for creating a\nara::log::LogStream\nobject which is then sub-\nsequently filled with message content (i.e. message arguments). Alternatively to\nara::log::Logger::WithLevel\n, there are also separate member functions for\ncreating a\nara::log::LogStream\nobject, one per supported log level.\nArguments are added to a verbose message by calling an appropriate\noperator<<\noverload for the desired argument:\nlogger.WithLevel(LogLevel::kInfo) << \"text\" << 4.2;\nThe\nara::log\nFunctional Cluster defines such\noperator<<\noverloads for all C++\narithmetic types, for bool, for string types, and for a number of\nara::core\ntypes.\nApplication-defined data types can be logged as well, by providing suitable\nopera-\ntor<<\noverloads for them.\nPlease note that there is no\noperator<<\noverload for char, as it might conflict with\nthe overloads for\nstd::uint8_t\nor\nstd::int8_t\n. The behavior of logging a single\nchar is therefore implementation-defined and will often, but not necessarily, output the\nordinal value of the char as an integral value.\nAs a workaround, the\noperator<<\noverload for\nara::core::StringView\ncan be\nused in order to log a single-char string.\nAs the application model allows annotating arguments with attributes, the\nara::log\nAPI for non-modeled messages also supports this. Arguments of certain types can be\nannotated with a name and possibly also a unit attribute. For instance:"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "3\n<< Arg(4.2, \"velocity\", \"m/s\");\nThe string argument text is annotated with a name attribute called identifier. The\ndouble argument 4.2 is annotated with a name attribute velocity and a unit of m/s.\nThese attributes can only be set for some of the built-in types that the\nara::log\nAPI\nsupports, i.e. all arithmetic types, bool, strings, and raw data blobs.\nNon-modeled messages can also contain information about the location of the log\nmessage call in source code. For this purpose, the member function\nara::log::\nLogStream::WithLocation\nis called with the filename and line number of the call\nsite. These should usually come from the compiler-defined\n__FILE__\nand\n__LINE__\nsymbols:"

This API returns a\nara::\nlog::LogStream\nobject that has to be used by passing arguments via the insert\nstream operator<<.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003, RS_LT_00049)\n[SWS_LOG_00013]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nTo initiate a\nLog message\nwith the Log level\nVerbose\n,\nthe API\nara::log::Logger::LogVerbose\nshall be called. This API returns a\nara::log::LogStream\nobject that has to be used by passing arguments via the\ninsert stream operator<<.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003, RS_LT_00049)\n[SWS_LOG_00130]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nTo write a Log message with a programmatically deter-\nmined log level, the API\nara::log::Logger::WithLevel\nshall be called.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nLT_00003, RS_LT_00049)\nStore LogStream objects in a variable\n:\nIt is also possible to use the\nLogging API\nin an alternative way by storing a\nara::\nlog::LogStream\nobject locally in some named variable. The difference to the tem-\nporary object is that it won't go out of scope already at the end of the statement, but\nstays valid and re-usable as long as the variable exists. Hence, it can be fed with\ndata distributed over multiple lines of code. To get the message buffer processed by\nthe\nLogging framework\n, the\nara::log::LogStream::Flush\nmethod needs to\nbe called, otherwise the buffer will be processed when the object dies, i.e. when the\nvariable goes out of scope, at the end of the function block.\nPerformance remark\n:\nDue to the fact that a\nara::log::LogStream\nis no longer created per message but\nrather could be re-used for multiple messages, the costs for this object creation is paid\nonly once  per log level. How much this really influences the actual performance\ndepends on the\nLogging framework\nimplementation. However the main goal of this\nalternative usage of the\nLogging API\nis to get the multi-line builder functionality.\n25 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"

      "verbatim_text": "2\nmLog.LogInfo() << Arg(43, Hex(4));\nuses\nara::log::Hex\nto add the hint to the message that this argument is supposed\nto be displayed as a hexadecimal value. The second line additionally adds the hint that\nthe hexadecimal number should be displayed with four digits.\nOther functions exist that allow to format as binary, decimal, or octal values, and to\nformat floating-point values in different ways and with specific precisions.\nIt is the decision of the viewer application whether to heed these hints.\n7.3.2 Modelled messages\nThe\nara::log\nFunctional Cluster defines a single member function\nara::log::\nLogger::Log\nfor sending modeled messages. Unlike the non-modeled message\nAPIs, it represents a single-call interface, i.e. a single function call passes all argu-\nments to the\nara::log::Logger\ninstance and performs all necessary actions to\ngenerate and send the message.\nThis has the advantage that the runtime cost for a modeled message that is eventually\nnot being output (because the message's log level does not reach the configured log\nlevel threshold) can be made very small: after parameter passing and function call, a\nsingle\nif\nclause checks the log level threshold and immediately returns if the threshold\nis not reached. This contrasts with the non-modeled message APIs, where multiple\nfunction calls are performed for constructing a message object, even if that is then\neventually discarded.\n[SWS_LOG_00240]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nIf the API\nara::log::Logger::Log\nis called, the im-\nplementation shall use the\nDltMessage\nthat corresponds to the parameter\nMsgId\n.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003, RS_LT_00049)\n[SWS_LOG_00241]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nThe given argument types shall be verified during com-\npile time and a compile error shall be raised if they do not match to the modeled mes-\nsage argument types .\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003, RS_LT_00049)\n[SWS_LOG_00242]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nIf the configuration item\nDlt-\nLogSink.nonVerboseMode\nis false, all (modeled)\nDltMessage\ns sent to this\nDltLogSink\nshall be composed as verbose messages. Otherwise, non-verbose\nmessages shall be composed.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003, RS_LT_00049)\n7.3.2.1 Log message model\nAll modeled messages are defined as\nDltMessage\ns, which are aggregated by a\nLo-\ngAndTraceMessageCollectionSet\n. Each\nDltMessage\ncontains a\nmessageId\n,\n27 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nwhich needs to be unique within an ECU, and the\nmessageTypeInfo\ndenoting the\nlog level, and optionally the\nmessageSourceFile\nand\nmessageLineNumber\n. The\nDltMessage\naggregates an ordered list of\nDltArgument\ns, which in turn aggregate\nSwDataDefProps\nin the role\nnetworkRepresentation\n. The name of a log mes-\nsage argument is taken from the\nshortName\nof the\nDltArgument\n, while the type and\nunit are taken from the\nSwDataDefProps\n.\nAt design time it is possible to define an\nExecutable\nwith a\nSwComponentProto-\ntype\nthat has a\nPortPrototype\ntyped by an\nLogAndTraceInterface\n. Such a\nPortPrototype\nis used to describe that the\nSwComponentPrototype\nis able to\nforward logging information onto the external Dlt Log Viewer. The\nDltMessage\ns that\nare used by the\nSwComponentPrototype\nare collected in the\nLogAndTraceMes-\nsageCollectionSet\nthat is referenced from the\nPortPrototype\n.\nAt deployment time a mapping of the\nPortPrototype\ntyped by a\nLogAndTra-\nceInterface\nto a\nDltLogSink\nis described with the\nDltLogSinkToPortProto-\ntypeMapping\nthat takes a\nProcess\nof the\nExecutable\nas context into account.\nThe\nDltLogSink\nis referenced by the\nLogAndTraceInstantiation\nthat in turn\nis associated with the\nDltEcu\nthat carries the\necuId\n. The\nLogAndTraceInstan-\ntiation\nitself defines with\nsessionIdSupport\nwhether session IDs are used or\nnot. The\nDltLogSinkToPortPrototypeMapping\ndefines the\ndltSessionId\nand\ncontains a reference to\nDltContext\nthat defines the\ncontextId\nand the correspond-\ning\ncontextDescription\n. The\nProcess\nin which the\nExecutable\nis executed is\nassigned with the\nDltApplication\nthat defines the\napplicationId\nand the corre-\nsponding\napplicationDescription\n.\nThe\nDltLogSink\ndefines with the\ncategory\nthe type of the output sink:\nDlt-\nLogSinkRemote\n,\nDltLogSinkDlt\n,\nDltLogSinkFile\n,\nDltLogSinkConsole\n.\nIn case the\nDltLogSink\nhas the category\nDltLogSinkRemote\nto provide means\nto forward logging information to a Dlt log channel the\nlogChannelId\nis defined. In\ncase the\nDltLogSink\nhas the category\nDltLogSinkDlt\nto provide means to forward\nlogging information onto on a specific VLAN the\nendpointConfiguration\nis defined\nin addition to\nlogChannelId\n. The\nnonVerboseMode\ndescribes whether the modeled\nmessages will be sent as verbose messages as if they were non-modeled messages.\nIn case the\nDltLogSink\nhas the category\nDltLogSinkFile\nto provide means to\nforward logging information to a file in path of a file system a\npath\nis defined.       "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.3.2.2.2 Modeled message header file\n[SWS_LOG_00245]\n{DRAFT}\nModeled Message header file name\n⌈\nThe modeled\nmessage header file shall use the file name\nmessages.h\n.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003, RS_LT_-\n00049)\n[SWS_LOG_00246]\n{DRAFT}\nModeled Message header file existence\n⌈\nOne\nLo-\ngAndTraceMessageCollectionSet\nshall correspond with one modeled message\nheader file.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003, RS_LT_00049)\n[SWS_LOG_00247]\n{DRAFT}\nInclusion of modeled messages\n⌈\nThe symbols defin-\ning the modeled messages of one\nLogAndTraceMessageCollectionSet\nshall\nbe made exclusively available in the header file defined in [SWS_LOG_00245],\n[SWS_LOG_00246]\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003, RS_LT_00049)\nNamespaces are used to separate the symbols defined based on\nLogAndTraceMes-\nsageCollectionSet\nfrom each other to prevent name conflicts and they allow to use\nreasonably short names.\n7.3.2.2.3 Contents in the modeled message header file\nThe modeled message header file contains constexpr variable definition and corre-\nsponding type definition for the parameters of the API\nara::log::Logger::Log\n,\nand those definitions are defined inside user-defined namespaces to avoid variable or\ntype name collision.\n[SWS_LOG_00248]\n{DRAFT}\nNamespaces in the modeled message header files\n⌈\nBased on the symbol attributes of the ordered\nSymbolProps\naggregated by\nLo-\ngAndTraceInterface\nand\nLogAndTraceMessageCollectionSet.shortName\nin role namespace, the C++ namespace of the modeled message header file shall be:"

      "source_element": "SWS_LOG_00249",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 32,

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.5 Log and Trace Timestamp\nThe\nLog and Trace\ninformation is transmitted by means of the\nLT protocol\nwhich is bus agnostic.\nThis protocol offers the possibility to include a timestamp in each sent message,\nas long as such messages are sent with an extended header (refer to [7] for more\ninformation).\nThe synchronized time base is supplied by the Time Synchronization\nFunctional\nCluster\n. The\nnow()\nmethod is used by the\nAdaptive Application\ns in order to\nretrieve the current time from the TS (refer to [8] for more information).\nAccording to the requirement [TPS_MANI_03162], the reference time base is derived\nfrom the machine manifest\ntimeBaseResource\n.\n[SWS_LOG_00082]\n⌈\nLog and Trace\nshould have accesss to a synchronized time\nbase. The attribute\ntimeBaseResource\nin\nLogAndTraceInstantiation\nshall be\nused to identify the time base.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003)\n[SWS_LOG_00083]\n⌈\nIf the time base resource is referenced by the Log and Trace\nmodule in the manifest configuration\nLogAndTraceInstantiation\n.\ntimeBaseRe-\nsource\n, the current timestamp information shall be included in each DLT message,\notherwise not.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003, RS_LT_00017)\n[SWS_LOG_00091]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nWhen the\nCreateLogger()\nfunction is called,\nLog\nand Trace\nshall send a message, \"local time base used\" in case the used time base\nis a local time base or \"global time base used\" in case the used time base is a globally\nsynchronized time base.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003)\n36 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"

      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 37,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.6 Log and Trace data loss prevention\n[SWS_LOG_00095]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nWhen\nLog and Trace\nreceives simultaneously a high\nload of trace information generated by multiple\nAdaptive Application\ns, it shall\nbuffer this data internally to prevent the data loss during its continuous transmission.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00003, RS_LT_00030)\n7.7 Tracing\nTracing is crucial for a successful and effective application development and is needed,\nfor determination of the timing behavior of their Applications. Tracing of the behavior\nof the Adaptive Platform and of Adaptive Applications has paramount advantage when\nanalyzing information flow for numerous reasons, from debugging to measuring com-\nmunication latencies to profiling different communication events.\nLog & Trace introduces an overhead in the application. This overhead may influence\nthe behavior of the application and uses resources as memory, execution time etc. On\nthe other hand there are different uses cases during development of an application and\nrunning the application in the field. Thus sometimes it is necessary to log as many data\nas possible while the resources don't matter and sometimes the used resources have\nto be as little as possible. To achieve different goals, the different configurations of the\nLog & Trace should be considered. These configurations include:\n•\nPrecompile configuration,\n•\nStatic configuration,\n•\nDynamic configuration.\nThe precompile configuration configures the Log & Trace that none or minimal runtime\noverhead does exist in the application. Dedicated trace points can be enabled or dis-\nabled before the building of the application. Even so it is possible to configure trace\npoints to use special trace capabilities of the environment. This guarantees minimal\nruntime overhead during the tweaking performance of the system. The static config-\nuration is part of the deployed application. Certain configuration items i.e. the Log &\nTrace sinks that are not changeable when the application is running. Checks or ini-\ntialization is done once when the application is started. The dynamic configuration\nintroduces the most overhead because the checks or initialization has to be done each\ntime a Log & Trace is called.\nThe trace methods are integrated in the ara::log Functional Cluster. For AUTOSAR\napplications the trace is identical to the use of the API for modeled messages. This\nchapter specifies internal handling of the trace to provide a clear interface between the\nAUTOSAR stack vendor and the trace tool vendor. It further shows special adaptions\nand specifies the configuration of the\nARTI-trace\n.\n37 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"

      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.3: Overview of Tracing\n7.7.1 OS/ara::log Adapter\nThe OS/ara::log Adapter adapts the trace functionality of the operating system to\nara::log. The OS/ara::log Adapter is specified in [9, SWS\nOperatingSystemInterface] chapter OS/ara::log Adapter.\n7.7.2 Precompile configuration of ara::log/Trace\nThe ara::log/Trace is configured with precompile configuration to allow only minimal\nor no overhead in the running application.       "source_page": 42,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThe\nTraceSwitch\nis generated by the code generator of the AUTOSAR-Stack vendor.\nThe generated header file should be located in the same directory where the modeled\nmessages are located.\n7.7.3 Static configuration of ara::log/Trace\nModeled\nara::log\nmessages can be routed to ARTI trace as additional log sink beside\nconsole, file and network. This allows the trace to be configured statically. The ARTI\ntrace can be switched on and off without recompiling the application.\n[SWS_LOG_20005]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nWhen\nDltLogChannel.logTraceLogMode\nis set\nto\nkArti\n, then the\nara::log::Logger::Log\nshall call\nara::log::ext::\nTraceArti\nwith all variadic parameters.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00059, RS_LT_00060, RS_LT_-\n00061, RS_LT_00062)\nThe call of\nara::log::ext::TraceArti\nshould be done before the message is\nbeing formated or filtered by the verbosity because the filtering for ARTI is done by the\ngenerated\nara::log::ext::TraceArti\nor by the trace tool itself.\n7.8 Output Bindings\n7.8.1 Overview\nLog and Trace\nhas built-in support for console output and file output. In addition to\nthat, it supports a remote backend, which represents a network-based sink. A typical\nchoice on an AUTOSAR Machine is the\nLT protocol\n, but other backends can also\nbe supported by vendors.\nThis section defines the mapping of the abstract\nara::log\nAPI to such backends.\n7.8.2 Console binding\n7.8.2.1 General\nThe console output binding is set by using the value\nDLT_LOGSINK_CONSOLE\nfor a\nDltLogSink\nreferenced by\nLogAndTraceInstantiation\n.\nPlease note that many aspects of the console output are currently implementation-\ndefined. This includes, for instance, the general layout of messages, the format of\ntimestamps, and which elements from the DLT message header are being output at\nall.\n[SWS_LOG_00227] Newline addition in console output\n⌈\nThe\nLogging frame-\nwork\nshall append an EOL sequence to each message in console output.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_-\n00002)\n42 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P43_73",
      "source_element": "SWS_LOG_00228",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 43,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.8.2.2 Message arguments\n[SWS_LOG_00228] Argument separation in console output\n⌈\nWhen a message\ncontains more than one payload argument, any two payload arguments shall be sepa-\nrated by a single space character (U+0020) in console output.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00002)\nExample: A log call such as:\nmLog.LogInfo() << \"speed\" << 4.1 << \"m/s\";\nwill result in this output:\n... speed"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P43_74",
      "source_element": "SWS_LOG_00228",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 43,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": " represents a single space character.\n[SWS_LOG_00229] Display of argument attributes in console output\n⌈\nIf a payload\nargument contains a name attribute, then the name attribute shall be prepended to\nthe argument value, and separated from the value with a colon character (U+003a). If a\npayload argument contains a unit attribute, then the unit attribute shall be appended\nto the argument value, and separated from the value with a colon character (U+003a)\nas well.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00056, RS_LT_00002)\nExample:\nspeed:42.1:km/h\n, where speed is the value of the name attribute, and\nkm/h is the value of the unit attribute\nThe following subsections details how the data types that are supported by the ara::log\nAPI are being represented in console output.\n7.8.2.2.1 bool\n[SWS_LOG_00230] Console output of bool values\n⌈\nA message argument value\nof\nbool\ntype shall be output to console as the string 0 (U+0030) for\nfalse\n, or 1\n(U+0031) for\ntrue\n.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00002)\n7.8.2.2.2 ara::core::Span<const ara::core::Byte>\n[SWS_LOG_00231] Console output of raw binary data\n⌈\nA message argument value\nof type\nara::core::Span<const ara::core::Byte>\nshall be output to console\nas a sequence of hexadecimal octets separated by apostrophe characters (U+0027).\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00002)\nExample:\n48\u001f65\u001f6c\u001f6f\n43 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P44_75",
      "source_element": "SWS_LOG_00232",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 44,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.8.2.2.3 InstanceSpecifier\n[SWS_LOG_00232] Console output of InstanceSpecifier values\n⌈\nA message argu-\nment value of type\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nshall be output to console as\nthe result of calling\nInstanceSpecifier::ToString\n.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00002)\n7.8.2.2.4 std::chrono::duration\n[SWS_LOG_00233] Console output of std::chrono::duration values\n⌈\nA mes-\nsage argument value of type\nstd::chrono::duration\nshall be output to\nconsole as a decimal integer value, followed by the duration's unit in SI notation,\nfor at least these unit dimensions:\nstd::nano\n,\nstd::micro\n,\nstd::milli\n,\nstd::centi\n,\nstd::deci\n,\nstd::ratio<1>\n,\nstd::deca\n,\nstd::hecto\n,\nstd::kilo\n,\nstd::mega\n,\nstd::giga\n.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00002)\nNote: The SI metric prefix for micro may be µ or simply u.\nExample:\n42ns\n7.8.3 File binding\nThe file output binding is set by using the value\nDLT_LOGSINK_FILE\nfor a\nDlt-\nLogSink\nreferenced by\nLogAndTraceInstantiation\n.\nThe appearance of the file output is currently implementation-defined.\n7.8.4 DLT binding\n7.8.4.1 General\nAn output binding for the DLT protocol is set by using the value\nDLT_LOGSINK_NETWORK\nor\nDLT_LOGSINK_DLT\nfor a\nDltLogSink\nreferenced\nby\nLogAndTraceInstantiation\n.\n7.8.4.2 Log level\nThe\nLT protocol\nsupports the exact same log levels as\nara::log\ndoes. There is\ntherefore a 1:1 mapping of\nara::log\nlog levels to\nLT protocol\nlog levels.\n[SWS_LOG_00234] Translation of log levels\n⌈\nA log level attribute of a\nDltMessage\nshall be translated into the\nLT protocol\nlog level with the same name.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_-\n00002)\n44 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P45_76",
      "source_element": "SWS_LOG_00235",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 45,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.8.4.3 Message arguments\nThe following subsections details how the data types that are supported by the ara::log\nAPI are being represented in the\nLT protocol\n.\n7.8.4.3.1 bool\n[SWS_LOG_00235] DLT output of bool values\n⌈\nA message argument of\nbool\ntype\nshall be output as a DLT message payload argument of type BOOL.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00002)\n7.8.4.3.2 string types\n[SWS_LOG_00236] DLT output of string values\n⌈\nA message argument of type\nconst char\n*\nor\nara::core::StringView\nshall be output as a DLT message pay-\nload argument of type STRG, with TYFM set to UTF-8 encoding.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00025, RS_-\nLT_00002)\n7.8.4.3.3 ara::core::Span<const ara::core::Byte>\n[SWS_LOG_00237] DLT output of raw binary data\n⌈\nA message argument of type\nara::core::Span<const ara::core::Byte>\nshall be output as a DLT message\npayload argument of type RAWD.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00002)\n7.8.4.3.4 InstanceSpecifier\n[SWS_LOG_00238] DLT output of InstanceSpecifier values\n⌈\nA message argument\nof type\nInstanceSpecifier\nshall be output as a DLT message payload argument\nof type STRG, with TYFM set to UTF-8 encoding, consisting of the result of calling\nInstanceSpecifier::ToString\n.\n⌋\n(RS_LT_00002)\n45 of 93 Document ID 853: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace"
    },

    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P57_110",
      "source_element": "SWS_LOG_00173",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 57,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8.3 Class definitions\n8.3.1 Class LogStream\nThe class\nara::log::LogStream\nrepresents a\nLog message\n, allowing stream op-\nerators to be used for appending data.\n[SWS_LOG_00173]\n{DRAFT}\nDefinition of API class ara::log::LogStream\n⌈"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P57_111",
      "source_element": "SWS_LOG_00173",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 57,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "⌋\n(RS_LT_00003)\nNote:\nNormally\nApplication process\nes would not use this class directly. Instead one of\nthe log methods provided in the main\nLogging API\nshall be used. Those methods\nautomatically setup a temporary object of this class with the given log severity level.\nThe only reason to use this class directly is, if the user wants to hold a\nara::log::\nLogStream\nobject longer than the default one-statement scope. This is useful in order\nto create log messages that are distributed over multiple code lines. See the\nara::\nlog::LogStream::Flush\nmethod for further information. Once this temporary ob-\nject gets out of scope, its destructor takes care that the message buffer is ready to be\nprocessed by the Logging framework.\n8.3.1.1 Extending the Logging API to understand custom types\nThe\nara::log::LogStream\nclass supports natively the formats stated in chapter\n8.2, it can be easily extended for other derived types by providing a stream operator\nthat makes use of already supported types.\nExample:"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P58_112",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 58,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P59_113",
      "source_element": "SWS_LOG_00039",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 59,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8.3.1.2 LogStream::Flush\n[SWS_LOG_00039]\n{DRAFT}\nDefinition of API function ara::log::Log\nStream::Flush\n⌈"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P59_114",
      "source_element": "SWS_LOG_00039",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 59,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "⌋\n(RS_LT_00003)\nNote:\nCalling\nara::log::LogStream::Flush\nis only necessary if the\nara::log::\nLogStream\nobject is going to be re-used within the same scope. Otherwise, if the\nobject goes out of scope (e.g. end of function block) then the flushing operation will\nbe done internally by the destructor. It is important to note that the\nara::log::\nLogStream::Flush\ncommand does not empty the buffer, but it forwards the buffer's\ncurrent contents to the\nLogging framework\n.\n8.3.1.3 Built-in operators for natively supported types\n[SWS_LOG_00040]\n{DRAFT}\nDefinition of API function ara::log::Log\nStream::operator<<\n⌈"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P60_115",
      "source_element": "SWS_LOG_00041",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",

      "source_page": 68,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8.3.2 Class Logger\nThe class\nara::log::Logger\nrepresents a logger context. The\nLogging frame-\nwork\ndefines contexts which can be seen as logger instances within one\nApplica-\ntion process\nor process scope.\n[SWS_LOG_00172]\n{DRAFT}\nDefinition of API class ara::log::Logger\n⌈"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_log_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_L_P68_141",
      "source_element": "SWS_LOG_00172",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
      "source_page": 68,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "⌋\n(RS_LT_00003)\nThe contexts have the following properties:\n1) Context ID\n2) Description of the Context ID\n3) Default log level\nA context will be automatically registered against the\nLogging back-end\nduring cre-\nation phase, as well as automatically deregistered during process shutdown phase.\nSo the end user does not care for the objects life time. To ensure such housekeeping\nfunctionality, a strong ownership of the logger instances needs to be ensured towards\nthe\nLogging framework\n. This means that the\nApplication process\nare not\nsupposed to call the Logger constructor themselves.\nThe user is not allowed to create a Logger object by himself. Logger context needs to\nbe created by the provided API call\nCreateLogger()\n.\n8.3.2.1 Logger::LogFatal\n[SWS_LOG_00064]\n{DRAFT}\nDefinition of API function ara::log::Logger::LogFatal\n⌈"
    },
    {

    },

      "verbatim_text": "This meta-class represents the Context that groups Log and Trace Messages that are generated by an\napplication.\nTags:\natp.recommendedPackage=DltContexts"

      "source_page": 90,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nB Platform Extension API (normative)\nThe focus of the APIs in this section are for OEM-specific platform extensions. The\nabstraction of the interfaces is lower which could lead to a higher machine dependency\nB.1 Tracing Interface in ara::log\nThe tracing interface is not for applications. It is internally used in ara::log to provide\nan interface for external trace tools.\nB.1.1 TraceArti\n[SWS_LOG_20000]\n{DRAFT}\nDefinition of API function ara::log::ext::TraceArti\n⌈"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Log and Trace\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nC Change History\nPlease note that the lists in this chapter also include specification items that have been\nremoved from the specification in a later version. These specification items do not\nappear as hyperlinks in the document.\nC.1 Change History of this document according to AUTOSAR Re-\nlease R23-11\nC.1.1 Added Specification Items in R23-11"

  "bisheriges_fragment": "<div class=\"ai module-guide\"><p class=\"ai-note\">Automatisch generierte Beschreibung, inhaltlich abgeleitet aus den referenzierten AUTOSAR-R25-11-Dokumenten (SWS-Spezifikation und begleitende Standarddokumente) — kein offizieller AUTOSAR-Text. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h3>Rolle &amp; Verwendungszweck</h3><p>Der Functional Cluster Log and Trace (<code>ara::log</code>) stellt der AUTOSAR Adaptive Plattform und darauf ausgeführten Anwendungen ein einheitliches, hochperformantes Framework zur Erfassung von Diagnose-, Laufzeit- und Tracing-Informationen bereit <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#page=8\">SWS Log and Trace §1 „Introduction and functional overview“</a>. Primäres Ziel ist es, Entwicklern, Testern und automatisierten Diagnosesystemen detaillierte Einblicke in das Systemverhalten zur Verfügung zu stellen, ohne das Echtzeitverhalten der Applikationen durch blockierende I/O-Operationen zu beeinträchtigen <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00001\">[SWS_LOG_00001]</a>.</p><p>Das Modul standardisiert die Protokollierung auf Basis des branchenweiten DLT-Protokolls (Diagnostic Log and Trace, gemäß ASAM/AUTOSAR-Standard). Es ermöglicht die Weiterleitung von Log-Nachrichten über mehrere konfigurierbare Ausgabekanäle (Senken), darunter ein zentraler DLT-Daemon (zur Übertragung über Netzwerkschnittstellen wie Ethernet oder SOME/IP), lokale Ringspeicher/Dateien sowie die Systemkonsole <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00007\">[SWS_LOG_00007]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00176\">[SWS_LOG_00176]</a>. Zudem unterstützt <code>ara::log</code> ARTI-Tracepunkte zur genauen Zeiterfassung und Ablaufverfolgung von Threads und Prozessen <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#page=8\">SWS Log and Trace §1.1 „Architecture overview“</a>.</p><h3>Architektur- und Schnittstellenverträge</h3><p>Die Architektur von <code>ara::log</code> gliedert sich in Anwendungs-APIs, Kontextverwaltung und nachgelagerte Backend-Schnittstellen <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#page=8\">SWS Log and Trace §1.1 „Architecture overview“</a>:</p><ul><li><strong>Initialisierung (<code>InitLogging</code>):</strong> Anwendungen können ihre Logging-Umgebung explizit über <code>ara::log::InitLogging()</code> konfigurieren oder sich auf die deklarative Initialisierung über das Manifest verlassen <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00002\">[SWS_LOG_00002]</a>. Hierbei werden vierstellige App-IDs (z. B. <code>\"APP1\"</code>), eine Anwendungsbeschreibung sowie standardmäßige Log-Modi (<code>LogMode::kRemote</code>, <code>LogMode::kFile</code>, <code>LogMode::kConsole</code>) und globale Schwellwerte festgelegt.</li><li><strong>Kontexte und Logger (<code>CreateLogger</code>):</strong> Jede funktionale Komponente innerhalb eines Prozesses fordert über <code>ara::log::CreateLogger()</code> einen <code>Logger</code> für eine spezifische Kontext-ID (<code>CtxId</code>, z. B. <code>\"SENS\"</code> für Sensorik) an <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00005\">[SWS_LOG_00005]</a>. Logger-Instanzen besitzen eigene Beschreibungstexte und Schwellwerte (<code>LogLevel</code>) und sind referenzstabil.</li><li><strong>LogStream und Formatierungsoperatoren:</strong> Log-Nachrichten werden über typsichere Stream-Operatoren (<code>operator&lt;&lt;</code>) formatiert <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00129\">[SWS_LOG_00129]</a>. <code>Logger</code> stellt hierfür die Methoden <code>LogFatal()</code>, <code>LogError()</code>, <code>LogWarn()</code>, <code>LogInfo()</code>, <code>LogDebug()</code> und <code>LogVerbose()</code> bereit <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00018\">[SWS_LOG_00018]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00064\">[SWS_LOG_00064]</a>. Erreicht der geforderte Level nicht die aktive Filterschwelle, wird ein inaktiver Stream erzeugt, der alle Formatierungsoperationen ohne Allokationsaufwand überspringt.</li><li><strong>RAII-Flushing und Pufferung:</strong> Das temporäre <code>LogStream</code>-Objekt sammelt formatierte Tokens und überträgt die serialisierte Nachricht beim Zerstören am Ende des vollständigen C++-Ausdrucks über <code>Flush()</code> atomar in einen sperrenfreien Lock-Free-Ringpuffer <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00131\">[SWS_LOG_00131]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00132\">[SWS_LOG_00132]</a>. Ein separater Hintergrund-Thread übergibt die Pufferinhalte via IPC an den DLT-Daemon.</li></ul><p>Über DLT-Injektionsnachrichten kann der DLT-Daemon die Log-Level einzelner Kontexte oder der gesamten Applikation zur Laufzeit dynamisch verändern (<code>SetLogLevel</code>), ohne den Prozess neu starten zu müssen <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00201\">[SWS_LOG_00201]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00204\">[SWS_LOG_00204]</a>.</p><h3>Interaktionsfluss</h3><p>Der Interaktionsfluss einer Anwendung mit <code>ara::log</code> gliedert sich in Initialisierung, Kontextregistrierung, Stream-Verarbeitung und asynchronen Backend-Transport. Zur Laufzeit erfolgt die Filterprüfung (Early Exit) direkt im Aufruferthread; erst bei Überschreiten der Schwelle werden Zeichenketten und numerische Werte in den Stream serialisiert und via RAII übergeben.</p><div class=\"diagram\" id=\"diag-01\"><svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" viewbox=\"0 0 900 516\" font-family=\"Helvetica,sans-Serif\" style=\"max-width:900px\"><text x=\"450.0\" Filterschwelle</text><line x1=\"345\" y1=\"478\" x2=\"555\" y2=\"478\" stroke=\"#28251d\" stroke-width=\"1.1\" marker-end=\"url(#arrF)\"></line></svg></div><p class=\"diagram-note\">Interaktionsdiagramm: Initialisierung des Loggings, Erzeugung eines kontextbezogenen Loggers, RAII-basierte Nachrichtenformatierung über LogStream und asynchrone Weiterleitung an den DLT-Daemon sowie dynamische Schwellwertanpassung über Steuerkommandos. Quellen: <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00002\">[SWS_LOG_00002]</a>, <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00005\">[SWS_LOG_00005]</a> und <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00132\">[SWS_LOG_00132]</a>.</p><h3>Konfiguration &amp; Fehlerbehandlung</h3><p>Die Konfiguration von <code>ara::log</code> erfolgt primär im <code>LogAndTraceInstantiation</code>-Modell des AUTOSAR-Manifests. Dort werden AppID, Standard-Kontexte, Log-Senken (Remote, Console, File) sowie Puffergrößen und Verhalten bei Pufferüberlauf (Drop vs. Block) definiert <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00205\">[SWS_LOG_00205]</a>.</p><p>Hinsichtlich der Fehlerbehandlung verzichtet <code>ara::log</code> bei Standard-Log-Ausgaben bewusst auf Fehler-Rückgabewerte (Best-Effort-Prinzip), damit Logging niemals den primären Kontrollfluss unterbricht oder durch Ausnahmebehandlung gefährdet <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00006\">[SWS_LOG_00006]</a>. Sollte der interne Ringpuffer voll sein, greifen standardisierte Strategien zur Vermeidung von Datenverlusten oder Deadlocks <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_20000\">[SWS_LOG_20000]</a>:</p><ul><li><strong>Pufferüberlauf (Overflow Handling):</strong> Dropping ältester oder neuester Nachrichten mit automatischem Einbetten eines DLT-Überlauf-Markers (Message Loss Counter), sobald der Puffer wieder aufnahmebereit ist.</li><li><strong>Ungültige Kontext- oder App-Kennungen:</strong> IDs, die nicht den 4-Zeichen-ASCII-Konventionen entsprechen, werden auf standardisierte Ersatzbezeichner gemappt oder zur Compile- bzw. Init-Zeit abgefangen.</li><li><strong>Verbindungsabbruch zum DLT-Daemon:</strong> Die Applikation puffert Nachrichten lokal bis zur konfigurierten Kapazitätsgrenze und schaltet bei fortdauerndem Verbindungsverlust automatisch auf Backup-Senken (z. B. Konsole) um.</li></ul></div>\n",

  "bisheriger_wissensstand": {
    "wissen": [
      {
        "aussage": "ara::log stellt ein standardisiertes Logging- und Tracing-Framework auf Basis des DLT-Protokolls bereit.",
        "quelle": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace",
        "fundstelle": "SWS Log and Trace §1, SWS_LOG_00001"
      },
      {

Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Log and Trace als Routing-Schicht</h4><p><code>ara::log</code> leitet Nachrichten aus Anwendungen und Functional Clusters an konfigurierte Senken weiter. Anwendung und Kontext werden über IDs getrennt; der Schwellwert filtert die Schweregrade, bevor ein Backend Konsole, Datei oder Netzwerk bedient. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=section.7.1">SWS Log and Trace §7.1 „Necessary Parameters and Initialization“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=section.7.7">SWS Log and Trace §7.7 „Output Bindings“</a></p><div class="diagram" id="diag-01"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" viewbox="0.00 0.00 826.00 120.00" style="max-width:1101px">

href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/FO/AUTOSAR_FO_RS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=paragraph.4.2.4.2.4">FO RS LogAndTrace §4.2.4.2.4 „Filtering"</a>.</p><h4>Verhalten im Fehlerfall</h4>
<p>Fehler im Logging-Framework oder im darunterliegenden System sollen den Anwendungsprozess nicht beeinträchtigen: Die betreffenden Schnittstellen haben weder Rückgabewerte noch werfen sie Ausnahmen; Aufrufe werden bei einem solchen Fehler still verworfen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.6">SWS Log and Trace §7.1.6 „Initialization of the Logging framework“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00002">[SWS_LOG_00002]</a></p>
<p>Vor jeder Nutzung von <code>ara::log</code> ist <code>ara::core::Initialize()</code> erforderlich. Kann das Framework Nachrichten nicht verarbeiten, etwa weil die Daemon-Kommunikation noch nicht steht oder die Initialisierung noch nicht abgeschlossen ist, werden sie in einer durch <code>logSink.queueSize</code> begrenzten Queue abgelegt. Bei Überschreitung dieser Größe sind die ältesten Einträge zu verwerfen; dieselbe Regel gilt nach einem Daemon-Absturz. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.8.1">SWS Log and Trace §7.8.1 „Startup“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00001">[SWS_LOG_00001]</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.8.3">SWS Log and Trace §7.8.3 „Daemon crash“</a></p>

Quellen: <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.8.1">SWS Log and Trace §7.8.1 „Startup“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00001">[SWS_LOG_00001]</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.8.2">SWS Log and Trace §7.8.2 „Shutdown“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00123">[SWS_LOG_00123]</a>.</p>
<p>Nach <code>ara::core::Deinitialize()</code> muss die Anwendung die Logging-API nicht weiter verwenden und kann keine weiteren Nachrichten loggen. Das Framework muss zu diesem Zeitpunkt alle noch in der Queue befindlichen Nachrichten an die konfigurierten Log-Senken weitergeben. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.8.2">SWS Log and Trace §7.8.2 „Shutdown“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00123">[SWS_LOG_00123]</a></p>

Fehlerfall</h4> <p>Fehler im Logging-Framework oder im darunterliegenden System sollen den Anwendungsprozess nicht beeinträchtigen: Die betreffenden Schnittstellen haben weder Rückgabewerte noch werfen sie Ausnahmen; Aufrufe werden bei einem solchen Fehler still verworfen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.6">SWS Log and Trace §7.1.6 „Initialization of the Logging framework“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00002">[SWS_LOG_00002]</a></p> <p>Vor jeder Nutzung von <code>ara::log</code> ist <code>ara::core::Initialize()</code> erforderlich. Kann das Framework Nachrichten nicht verarbeiten, etwa weil die Daemon-Kommunikation noch nicht steht oder die Initialisierung noch nicht abgeschlossen ist, werden sie in einer durch <code>logSink.queueSize</code> begrenzten Queue abgelegt. Bei Überschreitung dieser Größe sind die ältesten Einträge zu verwerfen; dieselbe Regel gilt nach einem Daemon-Absturz. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.8.1">SWS Log and Trace §7.8.1 „Startup“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LogAndTrace.pdf#nameddest=SWS_LOG_00001">[SWS_LOG_00001]</a> <a class="docref"
